email_messages.body:
Hi Erin and David,

Sharing the final attendee list for next week’s Treasury Portal refresher (ACH templates + wire approvals). Please confirm your teams’ attendance by EOD Monday so I can lock the session size with Vendor Ops.

Proposed sessions (all times ET):
- Tue 10:00–11:00: Operations + Client Support
- Wed 2:00–3:00: Relationship Managers + Treasury Sales

Dial-in/Teams link: will send once headcount is confirmed.

Also: if there are any client-facing “how-to” PDFs you want included (e.g., Positive Pay exceptions, token reset), email them to me and I’ll compile into a single packet.

Thanks,
Marisol

Marisol Rivera
Treasury Services – Enablement
HarborPoint Community Bank

email_messages.subject: Re: Treasury Portal Training – final attendee list & dial-in
email_messages.body:
Marisol,

Confirmed on our side:
- Tue session: 6 attendees from Client Support (mix of new hires + 2 escalations specialists)

Request: can you spend 10 minutes on the “approval chain” configuration? We’re getting repeat tickets where a client adds an approver but doesn’t set limits/sequence correctly.

Erin—FYI, we’ll be using the training as part of onboarding for the two associates starting next Monday.

Thanks,
David

Manager, Client Support
HarborPoint Community Bank

email_messages.subject: Monthly compliance reminder: customer communication archiving
email_messages.body:
Hi all,

Quick reminder ahead of next week’s audit sampling: please ensure any customer-facing materials and operational communications are archived per the retention schedule.

Highlights:
- Final versions only (PDF) should be saved to the designated SharePoint library (no local-only copies)
- If a doc changes due to compliance language updates, store the superseded version in the “Archive – Prior Versions” folder
- For client support email templates/macros, export the current set once monthly and save the export file to the same library

If you need the folder path or permissions updated, send me the group name and I’ll coordinate with IT Access.

Thank you,
Marisol

Marisol Rivera
Treasury Services – Enablement
HarborPoint Community Bank

email_messages.subject: Q2 Campaign Performance Review — readout & next steps
email_messages.body:
Hi Erin and David,

Sharing the readout from yesterday’s Q2 marketing campaign performance review.

Key outcomes (Q2 vs Q1):
- Website form conversions: +12% (primary driver was improved landing-page flow + faster follow-up routing)
- Paid search: we paused the underperforming keyword set (the ones with high CPC and low form-completion rate) and will reallocate that budget into email nurturing (segmented sequences for treasury + lending leads).

Actions:
1) Marketing/Ops to shift remaining July paid-search budget into the nurture program by EOW.
2) David’s team to confirm the top two nurture journeys and SLA for lead handoff.

Side note for context: this is standard marketing performance management and isn’t connected to any compliance case work or due diligence-control investigations that have been circulating separately.

Thanks,
Marisol

Marisol Rivera
Director, Marketing Analytics
HarborPoint Community Bank

email_messages.subject: RE: Q2 Campaign Performance Review — readout & next steps
email_messages.body:
Marisol — thank you.

Can you confirm what we’re stating as the “outcome” for the Q2 review in the exec summary? I want to make sure we’re consistent before Kevin and I send the monthly update.

Also appreciate the note on keeping this separate from the compliance/due diligence items.

Erin

Erin McCarthy
VP, Marketing

email_messages.subject: RE: Q2 Campaign Performance Review — readout & next steps
email_messages.body:
Yes — for the exec summary, the outcome statement should be:

- Q2 review outcome: we delivered a 12% increase in website form conversions and, based on performance, paused underperforming paid-search keywords to reallocate spend into email nurturing (segmented lead nurture to improve conversion-to-appointment).

And agreed on separation: this is purely performance optimization; it’s not relevant to any compliance case investigations or the due diligence-controls allegation.

Marisol
